newsitem.title: UK: HSBC extends loss on Asia fears, off 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: HSBC extends loss on Asia fears, off 7 pct.

text.p: Shares in banking powerhouse HSBC Holdings Plc extended its losses on Friday afternoon, falling seven percent amid jitters over the Hong Kong dollar, market sources said.
At 1333 GMT, shares in HSBC, Asia's biggest bank, were down 161-1/2p at 21.72-1/2 stg in volume of two million.
Shares in Standard Chartered Plc, another bank with big Asia-Pacific region franchise, lost 41p or 3.9 percent at 10.11-1/2 stg.

Other bank shares held more tempered losses. Barclays Plc stock was off 14p at 14.05 stg, National Westminster Bank lost 16p to 801p, and Alliance & Leicester Plc rose 8-1/2p to 621p, helped by pleasing first-half earnings results.
"Looking around it seems as if people are playing the currency card," one analyst said, referring to the heightened selling in HSBC and Standard Chartered.
"If it is profit taking on top of that, then there will be more taken out of HSBC than Standard Chartered because it has recently outperformed more," he said.

HSBC shares fell in Hong Kong by HK$5 to HK$272 on Asian currency woes and fears that speculators would build up positions against the Hong Kong dollar, potentially hurting profits of banks in that market.
The Hong Kong market is shut on Monday for a public holiday.
